title: The Place Where Meaning Begins and Grows Without Saying

features.name: woven-row-cipher
features.desc-on-touch: Patterns planted in rows, each thread a word that learned to grow. The orchard reads itself backward and forward; meaning does not choose a direction.

features.name: textile-gate
features.desc-on-touch: Someone's cloth work hung as an entrance, its pattern a map of where meaning learned to make itself visible. You can read it or walk through it; it does the same thing.

features.name: silent-row-planting
features.desc-on-touch: Each stem holds a syllable that has learned not to speak. The pattern emerges only when you stop looking directly.

features.name: colour-field-memory
features.desc-on-touch: A swatch of dyed thread, years old, teaching younger threads how to remember the day they were made. The dye remembers the hand that applied it.

features.name: fence-line-that-grows-its-own-pattern
features.desc-on-touch: The boundary where the orchard decided to render itself as script. Meaning starting to ask: what form do I want to take?

inscription: here patterns learn to speak without sound, and the orchard reads the reader reading the rows

reverie.title: REVERIE — the weaver's field, afternoon
narr: You sit beside her as she stretches dyed thread between stakes.
She is teaching you the patterns without words, only showing.
Her hands know an alphabet the loom will understand.
You begin to see how the story lives in the colour order,
how the pattern itself remembers what needs to be said.

exits.label: back along the border where light stops and meaning continues its archive
deeper into rows where meaning learns to plant itself in stone
toward other clearings where weavers work without names
